S&P 500 Composite Index Daily Closing Level

Source: R/data.R
spx.Rd

The daily closing level of the S&P 500 Composite Index, spanning the period 2009-05-18 to 2020-12-31. This dataset is included as it is the series calibrated in the worked S&P 500 example, whose modified profile likelihood estimate places the critical time at 2020-03-03, at the onset of the COVID-19 crash. The window is the calibrated one and no more: 2,928 trading days, fitted on the first 2,428 with hold_out = 500 and fh = 500.

Usage

spx

Format

spx: A data.frame containing 2928 observations in 2 columns:

date

The trading date, of class Date.

close

The closing level of the index.

Source

Yahoo Finance, ticker ^GSPC, retrieved 2026-08-24 using quantmod::getSymbols(). The closing level is used; for an index the closing and adjusted-closing series are identical.

Details

The series is supplied as levels, not returns, because the LPPLS model is a model of the log-price path: fit_lppls() takes log(close) directly.

The original analysis used the CRSP S&P 500 Composite series (variable spindx, CRSP Stock Market Indexes, obtained through Wharton Research Data Services), which is licensed and may not be redistributed. The series shipped here is the corresponding Yahoo Finance series over the same trading days. The two agree closely: the trading calendars are identical over the window, the mean absolute relative difference in level is 1.6e-07, and the largest single-day discrepancy is 0.39 index points, on 2019-08-12. Recalibrating on this series leaves every reported quantity unchanged — the modified profile likelihood estimate \(\hat{t}_c = 2717\) (2020-03-03), \(m = 0.9\), \(\omega = 6.1596\), and all three likelihood intervals are identical; only the Brent-refined \(t_c\) at the final step of the MPL computation differs, in its seventh decimal place. That step refines thesis equation 38 at the \((\hat{m}, \hat{\omega})\) which minimise equation 39 on the integer grid.

Examples

# the log-price path the LPPLS model is fitted to
plot(spx$date, log(spx$close), type = "l",
     xlab = "", ylab = "log price", main = "S&P 500 Composite")


# the calibration window used in the worked example
n_cal <- nrow(spx) - 500
spx$date[n_cal]
#> [1] "2019-01-08"
